MAGICYOYO Responsive Yoyo V3, Professional Metal Yoyo for Kids Beginner, Aluminum Alloy Yoyo with Unresponsive Bearing + Bearing Removal Tool + Axle + Bag + 12 Yoyo Strings (Black Blue Purple) There was one summer in the very end of the 90s that I got into yo-yos. They boomed at my elementary school--so much so that eventually they were banned. After that ban, I wanted to see the fuss. I didn't get into them right away because many of my classmates were learning more advanced tricks by the time I realized the hype, and I figured I'd never get to that level. But during one fateful summer, away from the city for the whole season, I practiced on my own. I learned a few tricks, but that was it.

Fast-forward and I'm now seeing these toys more frequently downtown Chicago. From children to adults, the popularity is back. I did some research to see where I left off (quite a lot has happened), and looked up beginner-friendly yo-yos. I ordered this one and it's been played with daily since it arrived. It's very easy to use for someone like me who hasn't touched one in 20 years. There are different strings available, so no need to stress on back-ups just yet. There is also a bearing for an unresponsive mod, but I'm not there yet. So far, I've been able to re-do most of the tricks I learned, and I'm happy to see what else I'll learn with this one.
text_fidelity_b: MAGICYOYO Responsive Yoyo V3, Professional Metal Yoyo for Kids Beginner, Aluminum Alloy Yoyo with Unresponsive Bearing + Bearing Removal Tool + Axle + Bag + 12 Yoyo Strings (Black Blue Purple)

B. toys – Water Doodler Portable Drawing Board – Kids Painting Writing Doodle Board Toy – Perfect Travel Toys for Toddlers Non-Toxic – Color Doodle Drawing Game & Magic Water Pens The main thing that this toy reminds me of is invisible ink, though in reverse. Invisible ink made with lemon juice (see recipe below) starts out invisible, and can be made to "magically" appear. It's the opposite with this toy. When a child draws on this board, the drawing is initially visible, but it starts to fade within seconds, and it is completely gone within half a minute. Most children like to be able to see what they have drawn, as a complete drawing. Experiencing one's drawing disappear before one can even fully finish it is an exercise in sobbing futility for most young children.

Another comparison I'd make, and not to the favor of this toy, is that it is a poorly conceived remake of the classic toy, the [[ASIN:B00000J0HG Etch A Sketch]], which is a much better choice for no-mess drawing because, with that toy, the child's drawing does not go away until the child shakes the Etch A Sketch.

In my humble opinion, this toy is more geared toward caregivers than children because of its low mess-making potential. The pens don't leak, though it wouldn't matter if they did, because they are filled with water. It is also easy to tidy up this toy because it comes in a sturdy storage case with convenient handles.

Unfortunately, this is supposed to be a toy for children. Though it is certainly possible that some children will like this toy, I believe that many more will be frustrated. For that reason, I can't recommend it.

For those who are interested in an old-fashioned, inexpensive game of disappearing ink where children are less frustrated because they can make it reappear, here is a recipe:

1. Squeeze 1 tbsp. or so of lemon juice (either bottled juice, or juice of half a lemon) into a bowl and thin it with 1 tsp. of water.
2. Dip a Q-tip into the lemon juice mixture and use it to write a message onto a sheet of white paper.
3. Wait for the juice to dry completely, and watch it become invisible.
4. Show your secret message to a friend by heating the paper (safely!) by holding it close to an incandescent lightbulb. (Do NOT hold it near an open flame!)
text_fidelity_b: B. toys – Water Doodler Portable Drawing Board – Kids Painting Writing Doodle Board Toy – Perfect Travel Toys for Toddlers Non-Toxic – Color Doodle Drawing Game & Magic Water Pens

text_fidelity_a:
DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game This is a fun game. My boyfriend and I played it. It is only a two-player match game like tic-tac-toe or battleship. The youngest player starts and both players get two cards which they keep face down until the end of the game. The first player pushes out a cube in the top left corner of the game grid. The next player then pushes out another cube on the board with that same cube. The play continues with each player pushing out the next cube with the previous cube just played without using the same grid hole. The idea is to match five of the same characters in a row either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. When one player indicates a match, the losing player turns over their cards and if the character on one of the cards matches the winning players match, then that person now wins the game. If there is no match, then the winner keeps his win.

The game is simple, yet fun, and is full of strategy. There are two negatives, however. The game case is difficult to open and it feels like I am going to break off the plastic prongs when I pull it apart. Also, the game wobbles a bit when the outside "wings" are down. Third, it is easy to knock all the cubes out of the game grid. As my boyfriend was playing, he titled the game just a bit to see the characters better and many of the cubes fell out. Other than the lackluster quality of the game parts, the game itself is wonderfully simple and tremendous fun.
text_fidelity_b: DC Superheroes Top Trumps Match Board Game

My First Sewing Kit by Alex Crafts, Perfect for Beginners, Arts and Crafts Colorful and Fun Sewing Projects to Learn the Basic Skills of Sewing (Ages 7+) This possibly isn't the best starter kit for a child who has never sewn before. The instructions aren't that good. If the child has done any other sewing, or has anyone who can help (can be another kid) then this will provide a great deal of practice, which is where this really shines.

There are quite a few projects here. There is a draw string bag, a stuffed cat, a stuffed dog, a stuffed elephant, and a book cover with pencil holder wrapper.

For supplies, it has everything - scissor, tape measure, pins, pin cushion, button, even some extra stuff, like pop poms, that you won't need for any of the projects. There definitely is not even close to enough stuffing. It did not quite fill the cat, which is the first, and smallest, of the stuffed animal projects. You'll want to pick up something like [[ASIN:B000YZ7G44 Fairfield Poly-Fil Premium Polyester Fiber, White, 1 Bag, 12-Ounce]]. Any fiberfill will do, but this is a good one, similar to what is in the kit. While on the topic of stuffing, a double pointed knitting needle, or better http://www.amazon.com/Little-Foot-That-Purple-Thang-/dp/B001ELBCFG/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1464647654&sr=8-1&keywords=purple+thang will help get the stuffing into the tight areas, like the tails. Both the fiberfill and the thang will be useful items in a variety of sewing projects.

For the embroidery floss, it says to cut the skein on one side to make lengths. That works, no issue, but it might be better to make a little yarn butterfly (really simple; instructions are online) so that you can pull the length you need for each section and the leftovers, and there will be plenty, can be used to make friendship bracelets. There is an excess of embroidery floss here.
text_fidelity_b: My First Sewing Kit by Alex Crafts, Perfect for Beginners, Arts and Crafts Colorful and Fun Sewing Projects to Learn the Basic Skills of Sewing (Ages 7+)

text_fidelity_a:
Kiddieland Lights 'N' Sounds Space Blaster,Multi Perfect item for toddlers who are stuck in that quirky place.. between infant toys not peaking or holding their interest yet, toddler toys are a bit cognitively too hard!! At 18mo. This is the perfect size being its lower profile.. for a little to play without your help! They can climb on/off and scoot a few feet.. if they tumble or bump off, no worry of injury with adult supervision and used on carpet.

Ours is entertained by anything he can load and unload on his own.. Ohh, and pushable buttons seem just too much for him!! This space blaster delivers in spades.. he’ll mount up scoot a few ft. all just to get up and meticulously load in items around the house into the seat! Then, repeat the process stop- and time to unload his haul! Before each scoot.. he moves through a button sequence with the gadgets provided on the dash… he even removes spaceman and puts into the seat- filling up the “under the hood” as well.. This $38 item has provided us our longest entertainment yet at this awkward stage.

Downside components noticed: this does not have a mute button!!! If turned on you get both lights ans sounds- Would love ability without sound when using dash controls- as the sounds get daunting!! I recommend indoor use only and although this can in theory function outdoors.. I find it’s not made for outside elements! Concrete rips up plastic tires fast and any water sprinkler, rain, etc will bring it to an early demise..!! (If used outdoors place on grass + bring inside after use!)

A quirky toy for that awkward phase and one I’d recommend.. it’s not the element of riding that entertains- but, rather what can be done while maneuvering!! Hoping this info can help your decision- stay safe.
text_fidelity_b: Kiddieland Lights 'N' Sounds Space Blaster,Multi

Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players This is a very cute concept and something out-of-the-ordinary for a board game! The object of the game is to make it out with the least amount of goo on your shoe. This is represented by actual pieces of putty that you place on the board and squish with your pawn as you land on a square (thus sticking the goo to your, erm, shoe).
My kids really enjoyed it, but I can't help feeling like there are some design flaws that could have been prevented. For example, the spinner needs to be deconstructed to put away in the box. The way the board folds (see picture), the crease is over the spinner area, and with the bars on the spinner (which I like, as it looks like a playground toy) won't fit, which means you have to totally take that apart and rebuilt it each time. On that note, it isn't much of a spinner at all, but just a wheel. There is no clicker or arrow that sticks out to slow it down as it spins... it basically spins until momentum from your push wears out, sort of like spinning a top. It takes a while to finally stop on its own, which makes the game feel like it is moving slowly. I was very tempted to just stop it manually a few times, but that might bring up the possibility of cheating.
Meanwhile, I wish the goo had more colors, or at least colors that matched the shoes in the game. I can say on the positive note, the goo is very kid friendly!
My daughter lost one of the colors and it turns out she was SITTING on it and it was all stuck in her dress. I suddenly had flashbacks of when silly putty got stuck on her clothing and bed and we had to toss them both because it never came off... but this stuff comes off! It easily rolls into balls with your fingers and comes right off clothing in the process. So, definitely some extra points for that! I just wish the game board and spinner were designed a little better, that would make it a lot more fun to play (and put away!).
text_fidelity_b: Goo on My Shoe - Silly, Sticky Family Board Game - Made by Kids for Kids - for Ages 4+ - 2-4 Players

LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit Holy Crap Yes! We are a family of Lego Maniacs and this set is wonderful. I have a fifteen year old and we recently got the newest Millenium Falcon and I had a realization that his abilities were quite beyond that set, and most sets out there, so I started looking at the expert and Technic sets. This set was perfect, it is a step up in challenge and scope from the standard sets. It was great to watch him to tear into the bags and deliberately build. Not only was it a little more challenging, but the scope if far more impressive. The set itself is huge, and the architectural elements are involved although somewhat repetitive.

We worked on this over several days and we are quite happy with the results. The build is detailed and has some very interesting pieces. Especially nice are the clock faces that are beautiful. The back printing on the clear disk gives them a gem like quality, they are sharp clean and wonderfully graphic. Absolutely beautiful. Also impressive are the scores of micro figures (usually found in Lego games.) Long term, I'm not sure that we will ever need this many tan microfigures on any build, but interesting piece. Also nice are the literally hundreds of architectural detail pieces from the little teeth pieces to the spires.

We actually looked up photos of Big Ben and we are astounded at the details. It is a wonderful representation of the end of the building. If I had anything negative to say about the build it would be that it is a bit of a façade for that end of Westminster. Which is forgivable given all the detail and how many pieces (and space) it would take to make the whole building.

All in all, this was an incredible build. I'll try to get the time lapse up when I can get it edited.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

However, they were definitely firmly and securely packaged in there and were not going anywhere or getting damaged with those vacuum formed spots to sit.

text_fidelity_a:
Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity It's not wide enough to make a scarf, not for most kids. There is very little yarn included. You will need worsted weight for this kit.

The last point leads into my main issue with this. It does not provide enough information. You know you need yarn, but yarn varies in weight from lace (even gossamer) to super bulky. These terms refer to how thick the yarn is. Buy too thin, and the project will look terrible. Buy too thick and the yarn won't fit into the weft holes. You need worsted weight, and the only reason I know this is I knit and I recognized the yarn. The kit doesn't tell you.

If you hit a knot in the yarn, as I did, you should not keep going. Cut at the end of the row (the instructions don't tell you this) then start on the right side again (the instructions don't tell you this) and whenever you stop or start, leave a tail long enough to weave in later (nothing about weaving in tails is covered -- you're just supposed to know how to do that).

If you want to do the purse, for example, cut 15 strands at 32 inches each (not explained) so that they turn into 16 inch strands when doubled. You can get away with cutting 16 inch and having them single stranded, but it isn't optimal, especially when you are tying pairs at the end. And maybe do it with a yarn not in this kit. They barely provide enough yarn in this kit, and no one wants their kid playing yarn chicken and getting upset. It's cheap yarn. Get a good amount.

When you start the yarn, it is shipped in a center pull ball. While the value of balls is explained a little (I suppose over leaving it in a loose skein or hank to tangle on itself) the concept of center pull isn't touched on. Dig into the ball and get the end inside. That way the ball stays still while you work.

You don't really need the tool to guide the yarn back and forth, but it should have come with a comb to push it down and keep it even, a trick especially hard when you move the piece along down the thread. That's perhaps the biggest design flaw in this. It tends to make the work uneven because it's slid and it leaves gaps where the next section starts. That can mostly be worked out by blocking the piece after (another technique not covered -- wet it, stretch it into the shape you want and even out the rows, and pin it down to dry.)

This is a great kit for someone who already knows a lot about yarn projects like crochet or knitting, or of course weaving. For a first yarn craft, a kid is going to need some help, ideally from someone who knows a lot about yarn projects.

MONILON 160 Pcs Magnet Building Sticks Kids Toys, Lengthen Magnetic Construction Building Blocks Set 3D Brain Training Learning Educational DIY STEM Toys The box says that this Magnet Building Sticks set is for ages six and up, but I'm really enjoying playing with it as an adult. I think younger kids would need some help to do the suggested building projects, but using the set to build things is easy. The set includes 120 magnetic sticks, 40 steel balls, and a gray bag with a drawstring to hold the set if you don't want to use the original packaging. The balls are 1 inch across, and the sticks are 2.25 inches long and 1/4 inch across.

The magnets hold together strong enough to basically stay where you put them but not so strong that it's difficult to pull things apart. The more stable builds (which have many triangles instead of squares) hold their shape well as you build them. Some of the building projects that have a more open structure have a tendency to collapse during certain stages of building, and then they start to attach to parts that they aren't supposed to. It can be a mess to straighten out. Once I realized that this could happen, I was more careful to stabilize these open structures as I built them, so this hasn't been a problem since.

The set also came with pictures of a number of projects. The pictures show only the finished building projects, but they were not always clear about what went where when the lines overlapped in the picture. Still, I've been able to do most of the projects, and of course you can come up with your own ideas. Kids may become frustrated trying to figure out the pictures and prefer to make their own building projects. Overall, I've had a lot of fun with this as have a teenager and a tween that have played with it.

I have some future modifications in the works already with higher DB antenna for the transmitter 3-axis Gimbal and a GoPro.

I would recommend this again to anyone looking to go in the medium area as far as quality drone but this build quality is quite good it feels and looks like a quality unit. There are those in my RC clubs that have some of these drones and have crashed them nothing more than maybe a propeller or some rotor guards now two of these people have the Meijer model previous mine DHS 700 and they fly them all the time one guy had like 10 batteries for the thing.

Owning this unit has renewed my desire and my love for the hobby and I'm looking forward to continuing exploring further with my hs700d great Job Holy Stone!
